items.headline: US air travel will not be back to normal until late Sunday, the FAA says, after 6,150 cancellations on Saturday followed 9,200 on Friday and a router installed by contractor L3Harris flooded 17 of the 22 en-route centres with connection attempts
items.matters: one bad router took down the national airspace, and Duffy now wants $50bn for air traffic telecoms.
items.body: WASHINGTON - The head of the FAA predicted that US air travel would not return to normal schedules until late Sunday as the aviation system gradually recovers from a nationwide flight shutdown that officials blamed on routine maintenance gone awry. As of 6:45 pm ET (23:45 GMT), airlines on Saturday had canceled more than 6,150 US flights and delayed more than 7,300, according to FlightAware, an aviation website. That followed about 9,200 flights canceled and 7,500 delayed on Friday after the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop because of disruptions to air traffic communications. FlightAware said more than 530 flights scheduled for Sunday were already canceled. Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford said on Saturday that he expected airline operations to largely return to normal by late Sunday. He also apologized for the disruption, adding that the system remains stable. The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours. It was the longest nationwide halt to air travel since the attacks of September 11, 2001 and one of the single worst US travel days ever. The issue prompted the White House to convene an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday and federal agencies to scramble to determine if it was a cyberattack. But the problem was traced to FAA contractor L3Harris' installation of at least one new router at a remote facility, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday. "We're working to determine whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router? We haven't determined what the fault was," Duffy told reporters at a news conference. L3Harris said it took the issue seriously and is supporting the FAA in its investigation. Its shares last traded down about 4% after hours on Friday. Duffy said the trouble began on Friday afternoon, when air traffic control centers experienced instability in radar and communications systems. The router issue led to data overloading other communications centers, officials said. "We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, and what that did was (it) gave us issues with our communication with airplanes, and it also caused some disruption with our radar," Duffy added. The issue affected communications at 17 of the FAA's 22 en route centers, which control aircraft during the cruise portion of a flight. Bedford said the FAA ordered the ground stop in case a center lost all communications. "No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost,"…

items.headline: US envoys floated Ukraine withdrawing from Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, Zelensky says, offering a national referendum if a full security and reconstruction package is on the table; the talks also produced a prisoner swap of more than 1,000 for more than 1,000
items.matters: first time territory has been formally linked to alliance membership in these talks.
items.body: Camera Icon US negotiators ?have flagged the idea of Ukraine withdrawing from the Donbas region. (EPA PHOTO) Credit: AAP US floats idea of Ukraine ceding Donbas for NATO club Olena Harmash Reuters 15 November 2026, 5:57am Copy link Share story US negotiators have floated the idea of Ukraine's withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy says, following the latest round of peace talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi. This is the first time the question of linking NATO membership to territorial concessions has been raised during the talks, Zelenskiy said in remarks to reporters released by his office on Saturday. "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?" he said. "That is why I believe NATO is back on the agenda. But you have also heard (Russian President Vladimir) Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation." Putin has long said Ukrainian membership of NATO is a red line for Moscow, citing the issue as one reason for launching Russia's full-blown invasion in 2022. Zelenskiy said Kyiv was not ready to concede territory but said that if it received a comprehensive package including security guarantees, the right to a strong and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question to a national referendum. Echoing comments made by European leaders at a summit in Dublin on Friday, Zelenskiy dismissed Russia's call for a broad agreement on European security architecture to be reached before the specifics are agreed on how to end the war in Ukraine. "We cannot turn everything upside down and start by talking about changing the security framework in the world or across the continent overall, and only then talk about ending this war. This war must be ended first," he said. US President Donald Trump's envoy Jared Kushner said the two sides had set out "maximalist positions" in the talks but in private discussions both "understand that practical compromises will be necessary to end this war". "Serious and constructive work continues among those of us committed to finding solutions," Kushner said in a social media post. Zelenskiy also dismissed Putin's suggestion for a local humanitarian ceasefire in Kostiantynivka, a hotly contested city in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region, saying it reflected Moscow's inability to take the city by force. items.headline: Tusk o drugim wecie: "Zadowoleni są hejterzy i pedofile"
items.summary: premier uderzył w prezydenta po zawetowaniu noweli wdrażającej DSA, Pałac Prezydencki odpowiedział, że obowiązujące przepisy wystarczą, a Krzysztof Gawkowski zapowiedział nową ustawę o bezpieczeństwie w sieci.
items.matters: Polska wciąż nie ma krajowej procedury szybkiego blokowania nielegalnych treści, której wymaga unijne rozporządzenie.
items.body: "Z prezydenckiego weta zadowoleni są hejterzy, rosyjskie farmy trolli, pedofile, ekstremalni nihiliści i lobbyści. Ofiarami tego weta są polskie dzieci, rodzice, bezpieczeństwo wszystkich obywateli. Tego nie da się w żaden sposób usprawiedliwić" - napisał w sobotę (14 listopada) na platformie X Donald Tusk. Do decyzji głowy państwa szef rządu odniósł się też w piątek, pisząc, że trudno wyobrazić sobie ważniejszą sprawę, która - jak stwierdził - powinna łączyć ponad politycznymi podziałami, niż ochronę dzieci przed internetowymi przestępcami . Do sobotniego wpisu premiera odniósł się rzecznik prezydenta Rafał Leśkiewicz. "Obowiązujące przepisy już dziś pozwalają zwalczać nielegalne treści w internecie. Prezydent jasno wskazał, co budzi jego zastrzeżenia- ordynarna próba ograniczania wolności słowa. Zamiast szukać winnych, zacznijcie stosować istniejące prawo i poprawcie wadliwą ustawę" - napisał. I dodał: "Zadziwiające, że w sprawie Trybunału Konstytucyjnego , dziś Uzurpacyjnego, wykazujecie się niezwykłą kreatywnością. Wobec patologii w Internecie nagle okazujecie się bezradni". Uzasadniając decyzję o zawetowaniu noweli, prezydent oświadczył, że nie będzie ulegał szantażom rządzących, tym bardziej, jeśli zakładnikami ma być bezpieczeństwo i wolność. Dodał, że państwo ma obecnie możliwość ochrony społeczeństwa w tym zakresie. Zawetowana ustawa była jedną z dwóch przygotowanych w odpowiedzi na prezydenckie weto nowelizacji ustawy o świadczeniu usług drogą elektroniczną oraz niektórych innych ustaw z początku roku. Wicepremier i minister cyfryzacji Krzysztof Gawkowski zapowiedział w piątek nową ustawę o bezpieczeństwie w sieci. Zaniepokojenie wetem prezydenta wyraziła też między innymi Państwowa Komisja do spraw przeciwdziałania wykorzystaniu seksualnemu małoletnich poniżej lat 15. Jej zdaniem weto oznacza "odsunięcie w czasie wdrożenia ważnych mechanizmów ochrony najmłodszych użytkowników internetu". Dodała, że ustawa przewidywała rozwiązania, które "mogły realnie wzmocnić tę ochronę", w tym między innymi skuteczniejsze reagowanie platform na nielegalne treści i ich blokowanie, mechanizmy weryfikacji wieku użytkowników oraz ocenę ryzyka związanego z funkcjonowaniem platform i usług…

items.headline: Redukcja wojsk USA w Europie mniejsza, niż zakładano
items.summary: Bloomberg: około 5 tys. żołnierzy zamiast nawet 25 tys., za to wzmocniona ma zostać wschodnia flanka; decyzja o stałej bazie USA w Polsce ma trafić do Trumpa 3-4 grudnia.
items.matters: los stałej bazy rozstrzyga się w tym samym przeglądzie, który tnie amerykańską obecność w Niemczech i Hiszpanii.
items.body: Administracja prezydenta USA Donalda Trumpa rozważa zmniejszenie liczebności amerykańskiego kontyngentu wojskowego w Europie. Jak informuje agencja Bloomberga, Waszyngton skłania się obecnie ku znacznie mniejszej redukcji, niż wcześniej zakładano. Zamiast nawet 25 tys. żołnierzy z kontynentu mogłoby zostać wycofanych około 5 tys. wojskowych. Amerykańscy żołnierze / Shutterstock Obecność amerykańskich wojsk w Europie od lat stanowi jeden z filarów bezpieczeństwa NATO. Teraz jej skala może się zmienić. Administracja Donalda Trumpa rozważa wycofanie około 5 tys. żołnierzy. Największe zmiany mogą dotknąć Niemcy. Dlaczego Waszyngton zmienia plany i jaki wpływ może to mieć na bezpieczeństwo Europy? Sprawdź, co wiadomo o planach Pentagonu. Najważniejsze informacje z kraju i ze świata znajdziesz na stronie głównej RMF24 Pentagon analizuje obecność wojsk USA w Europie Obecnie w Europie stacjonuje około 80 tys. amerykańskich wojskowych. Doniesienia o możliwym wycofaniu 25 tys. wywołały niepokój wśród europejskich sojuszników Stanów Zjednoczonych, dlatego Waszyngton skłania się obecnie ku znacznie mniejszej redukcji – o około 5 tys. żołnierzy. Jak wynika z doniesień Bloomberga, na zmianę rozważanego scenariusza wpłynęło kilka czynników. Jednym z nich jest zwiększanie wydatków na obronność przez europejskich członków NATO . Znaczenie ma również trwająca kampania militarna Stanów Zjednoczonych i Izraela przeciwko Iranowi . Pentagon bierze pod uwagę także strategiczne znaczenie amerykańskich baz wojskowych w Europie. Infrastruktura udostępniana przez sojuszników oraz europejska przestrzeń powietrzna są wykorzystywane przez USA podczas operacji wymierzonych w Iran. Mamy tu mnóstwo obiektów i sił, które znajdują się dokładnie tam, gdzie chcemy. Nie spodziewam się działań na dużą skalę – powiedział. Największa redukcja amerykańskiego kontyngentu może objąć Niemcy, gdzie znajduje się najliczniejsze skupisko amerykańskich żołnierzy w Europie. Jednocześnie NATO planuje wzmocnienie swojej obecności na wschodniej flance Sojuszu . Państwa graniczące z Rosją deklarują gotowość do współfinansowania kosztów utrzymania amerykańskich wojsk na swoim terytorium. Takie rozwiązanie mogłoby zachęcić Waszyngton do utrzymania, a nawet zwiększenia obecności wojskowej w tej części Europy. Ostateczna decyzja w sprawie liczebności amerykańskich sił w Europie będzie należała do Donalda Trumpa. Wcześniej zastępca sekretarza obrony USA ds. polityki Elbridge Colby ma przygotować raport dla szefa Pentagonu Pete'a Hegsetha. Zgodnie z przedstawionym harmonogramem 1 grudnia sekretarz obrony ma…

items.body: EDITION Türkçe English BHSC Pусский Français العربية Kurdî کوردی Shqip فارسی македонски Bahasa Indonesia Español US-Iran war Hormuz crisis Russia-Ukraine war WORLD TÜRKİYE ECONOMY POLITICS ENERGY TECHNOLOGY World Europe Polish premier rejects presidential talks on constitutional court crisis Donald Tusk says dispute over top court has been settled even as President Karol Nawrocki seeks cross-party consultations on Monday Jo Harper 14 November 2026 • Update : 14 November 2026 WARSAW ‘Matter of the Constitutional Tribunal has been settled,’ says premier Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said late Friday that he would not attend talks called by President Karol Nawrocki to resolve the country's escalating constitutional court crisis, insisting that the dispute over control of the institution has already been settled. Speaking to reporters in Dublin after a European summit, Tusk dismissed the need for further negotiations over the Constitutional Tribunal, whose leadership has been contested since an intervention at its Warsaw headquarters two weeks ago. "The matter of the Constitutional Tribunal has been settled," Tusk said, acknowledging that Nawrocki and opposition parties did not accept the new arrangements. "I am not waiting for the approval of those who for years were destroying the justice system in Poland," he added. Tusk said the court had resumed work and is on the path towards restoring its proper functioning. The refusal underscores the deepening confrontation between Tusk's pro-European governing coalition and Nawrocki, an ally of the opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, over the legitimacy of Poland's highest constitutional court. Nawrocki's office announced Thursday that representatives of all parliamentary political groups had been invited to consultations at Warsaw’s Belweder Palace on Monday. The Left (Lewica), a smaller coalition partner, announced that it would not participate, while Civic Coalition, Tusk's principal governing party, said the same. Representatives of the People's Party (PSL), Poland 2050, PiS, and the right-wing Confederation have indicated their willingness to attend. The confrontation escalated on Oct. 30 when police were deployed to the Constitutional Tribunal after a judge reported threats and disputed decisions emerged suspending Tribunal President Bogdan Swieczkowski and Vice-President Bartlomiej Sochanski. Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, a judge associated with the new majority on the court, subsequently assumed control of the institution. items.headline: Nowy sondaż: Zjednoczona Prawica 46,6 proc., Koalicja 15 X 41,3 proc.; model prof. Flisa daje prawicy 242 mandaty, czyli samodzielną większość
items.matters: hipotetyczny wspólny start obozu rządzącego przegrywa z hipotetycznym wspólnym startem prawicy.
items.body: W badaniu partyjnym przeprowadzonym na zlecenie Wirtualnej Polski Koalicja Obywatelska uzyskała 30 proc. wskazań i utrzymała pozycję lidera. PiS może natomiast liczyć na 15,5 proc. To wynik znacznie słabszy niż w poprzednich wyborach parlamentarnych . Pod progiem wyborczym znalazły się dwa ugrupowania współtworzące rząd: PSL z poparciem 4,5 proc. oraz Polska 2050, na którą chce głosować zaledwie 0,8 proc. respondentów. W takim układzie obecna koalicja rządząca miałaby poważny problem z utrzymaniem większości. Jednocześnie po prawej stronie sceny politycznej rośnie znaczenie Konfederacji i Konfederacji Korony Polskiej Grzegorza Brauna. Komentarze Artur Bartkiewicz: O tym, kto będzie rządził po 2027 r., mogą zdecydować PSL i Razem Najnowszy sondaż IBRiS dla „Rzeczpospolitej” pokazuje, że wiele musi się wydarzyć, aby wszystko pozostało po staremu. A o losach przyszłej większoś... Autorzy badania sprawdzili, jak wyglądałby podział poparcia, gdyby największe ugrupowania zdecydowały się na wspólny start. To scenariusz nawiązujący do dyskusji o konsolidacji poszczególnych ugrupowań i ewentualnym tworzeniu wyborczych sojuszy. W takim wariancie największe poparcie zdobyłaby Zjednoczona Prawica, skupiająca Prawo i Sprawiedliwość, ugrupowanie Rozwój Plus, Konfederację oraz Konfederację Korony Polskiej Grzegorza Brauna. Na wspólną listę tych formacji zagłosowałoby 46,6 proc. ankietowanych. Drugie miejsce zajęłaby Koalicja 15X, czyli porozumienie Koalicji Obywatelskiej, PSL, Polski 2050 i Nowej Lewicy. Taki wariant poparłoby 41,3 proc. badanych. Poza dwoma dużymi blokami wystartowałaby deklarująca konsekwentnie niechęć do sojuszy partia Razem, która uzyskała 5,8 proc. wskazań, przekraczając próg wyborczy. Niezdecydowanych było 6,3 proc. respondentów. Polityka PiS w koalicji z Braunem? 39 proc. Polaków nie wierzy w taki scenariusz 39 proc. Polaków nie wierzy w to, że PiS utworzy koalicję z Konfederacją Korony Polskiej Grzegorza Brauna – wynika z sondażu Pollster dla „Super Ex... Jeszcze wyraźniej różnicę między dwoma scenariuszami pokazuje prognozowany podział miejsc w Sejmie. Z wyliczeń opartych na modelu prof. Jarosława Flisa z Uniwersytetu Jagiellońskiego wynika, że wspólna lista ugrupowań prawicowych zdobyłaby 242 mandaty w 460-osobowym parlamencie. Oznaczałoby to możliwość samodzielnego utworzenia rządu. Koalicja 15X mogłaby liczyć na 212 miejsc, natomiast Razem wprowadziłoby do Sejmu sześciu posłów. Nawet po dodaniu mandatów partii Razem ugrupowania tworzące obecny obóz rządzący dysponowałyby łącznie 218 głosami. Do większości parlamentarnej zabrakłoby im zatem…

items.body: The S&P 500 gained 2.51% for the week to 7,561.67, snapping a four-week losing streak, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 2.27%, the Dow 2.07% (up 1,061.82 points) and the Russell 2000 1.32%. All eleven S&P 500 sectors finished higher, led by Energy (+5.42%), Industrials (+3.76%) and Communication Services (+3.72%). The week was front-loaded: Monday’s rally lifted the S&P 500 2.3% and the Dow 1,104 points, and the VIX dropped from 25.64 on Nov 6 to 19.92. By Friday, technology led the declines, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 3.4% and the Nasdaq-100 off 1.22%. The Dow was the only major index to rise on Friday. Two technology headlines also drew attention: Nvidia announced Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO on Thursday, and a Microsoft 365 outage disrupted services worldwide from Thursday until Microsoft reported full restoration on Saturday. Rates moved sharply. Treasury yields rose across the curve: the 2-year gained 36 basis points on the week to 4.89%, the 5-year 33 bp to 4.98%, the 10-year 29 bp to 5.15% and the 30-year 22 bp to 5.48%. October CPI (+0.4% m/m) and core CPI (+0.3%) both topped forecasts, and October PPI hit 6.5% year over year, the fastest since November 2022. Futures priced roughly an 88–92% chance of a 25 bp Fed hike on Dec. 8–9. Gold fell 4.63% on the week to about $3,886, silver fell 5.18%, WTI fell 2.50% and Brent 2.52%, the dollar index climbed 1.1% to about 103.4, and Bitcoin slipped below $70,000, trading near $68,300. items.body: Global markets enter the week of 16–20 November with a difficult combination of higher US bond yields, a stronger dollar, renewed questions about artificial-intelligence valuations and a changing oil supply picture. US technology stocks weakened at Friday’s close even as some European and Japanese benchmarks showed greater resilience. This weekend edition reviews the last completed traditional-market session and maps the economic and corporate events that may reset expectations when trading resumes. Published: Sunday, 15 November 2026 (GMT). Market-data reference: Friday, 13 November 2026 closing session unless otherwise stated. Research cut-off: Sunday, 15 November 2026, 03:17 GMT. Important: Sunday is not a regular cash-equity trading session; Friday’s prices below are historical closes, not live Sunday quotations. Cryptocurrency markets trade through the weekend. The figures below are deliberately anchored to the last completed trading session. Equity index observations are Friday closes; the US Treasury figures are official end-of-day par yields; the foreign-exchange reference is a central-bank fixing, not a live tradeable quote. Sources: FT market data ; Associated Press US index recap ; US Treasury daily yield curve ; Banque de France/ECB reference rates ; Reuters oil settlement reporting . Prices and yields are not all measured at the same moment. US yields have become the central transmission mechanism for several asset classes. The official ten-year Treasury par yield rose from 5.10% on Thursday to 5.15% on Friday; the two-year rose from 4.86% to 4.88%. When investors demand higher yields from government bonds, the discount rate applied to long-duration corporate cash flows generally rises. That tends to matter most for shares whose valuations rely on substantial expected profits many years into the future. The relationship is not mechanical. Higher yields can accompany stronger growth, and companies with robust immediate earnings may withstand them. But a simultaneous rise in yields, a strengthening dollar and weakness in highly valued technology creates a demanding backdrop. The test for next week is whether growth and earnings can justify valuations without relying on an easier financing environment. An official Nvidia filing states that the board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation, effective 11 November, and named chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive. Investors now need to assess both near-term execution and longer-term leadership continuity. This is distinct from the familiar debate over demand for AI…

The Nasdaq 100 outlook darkened on the same session as chips sold off: the S&P 500's tech gauge lost 1.7%, the weakest of the 11 major sectors, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 3.4%. One name ran through both the week and the final session: Nvidia. Both benchmarks snapped four-week losing streaks, per Reuters. The 10-year Treasury yield closed the week near 5.13%, per Investopedia. The week turned on Wednesday night, when Nvidia's board met to decide chief executive Jensen Huang's fate, per Al Jazeera. The New York Times had reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia vice president who reports to him, and Reuters reported a relationship with a second company employee. Huang stepped down on Thursday, days after reports surfaced of extramarital affairs, one involving a businesswoman US officials suspect of spying for China, per Reuters. The board named chief financial officer Colette Kress interim chief executive and Harvey C. Jones its first board chair. Nvidia's market value fell below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025, per Al Jazeera. Our November 11 report tracked the board's deliberations as they began. Nvidia shares plunged 10% over the first two days of trading this week, dropped another 4.3% on Thursday, per Investopedia, and fell a further 2% on Friday. The stock has now declined for six straight weeks, its longest streak since October 2012, per Reuters. The shares ended Thursday roughly 30% below their record high, per Investopedia. The bond market set the other half of the week's backdrop. October producer prices were up 6.5% on the year, the fastest annual rise since November 2022, per Reuters, though the monthly reading came in slightly cooler than expected. The print kept a December rate hike fully priced, with traders putting about a 14.5% chance on a 50-basis-point move, as of November 13, per Reuters and the CME FedWatch tool. items.body: Anthropic is selling 825M shares at $70 to $78 each, its latest prospectus shows . At the top of the range, the sale raises up to $64.4B. Demand is expected to leave some investors with fewer shares than they requested. Bloomberg reports that Anthropic plans to favor existing backers when allocating shares, according to bankers who have spoken with prospective buyers. The demand comes as investors pull back from AI stocks. Nvidia ( NVDA ) was down 3.4% as of 12:17 p.m. ET on Friday, following Jensen Huang's exit as its CEO this week. The Nasdaq 100 was down 1.8%. Nvidia is also one of Anthropic's backers in the deal. It plans to buy about $10B of shares in a $26B private placement at the IPO price, alongside Alphabet ( GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), TSMC ( TSM ), and others. Growth forecasts help explain the appetite. Goldman Sachs ( GS ), which leads the IPO with Morgan Stanley ( MS ), expects Anthropic's revenue to top $600B by 2030, Semafor notes . Anthropic's run-rate revenue, its recent sales annualized, reached about $81B as of October 31, up $10B in a month. At $78, Anthropic would be worth about $1.02T based on the shares outstanding after the IPO and the placement. Including stock options, restricted stock units, and shares reserved for employee plans, the valuation rises to about $1.4T, according to Bloomberg. Anthropic expects to set the final price on Wednesday, November 18. The shares are due to start trading on the Nasdaq the next…

For some dungeons, the new restriction missed the mark because of the overall level range of the enemies in the dungeon. items.body: Arctium App All News Arctium App Blue Posts Every Blizzard forum thread and news article we have tracked, newest first. 1 2 3 4 … 57 Raid Encounter Design in Season 3 Linxy Community Manager Nov 13, 2026 Post #1 Dungeons, Raids and Scenarios View on forums World of Warcraft EU Last week we made several adjustments to The Venomous Abyss with the intent of reducing the number of damage events that could kill you or your entire raid with a single individual mistake. We believe this type of severe mechanical penalty was used too often in The Venomous Abyss, causing the associated mechanics to become frustrating as the season wore on. Our goal with these changes was to ensure that damage events feel more proportional to player mistakes and to reduce the number of instances where individual mistakes could easily trigger group wipes. A couple examples from that list of changes: We feel that our design has shifted over time at the expense of the average Mythic player’s experience. Going forward into Season 3, we’d like to intentionally pull back on some of these severe mechanical penalties, even at the start of the season. Once Season 3 launches on the Public Test Realm, we’d like to invite you to test each difficulty of the new raid and see for yourselves. What is a “mechanical penalty”? Generally, when an encounter designer creates a mechanic, they also design a corresponding penalty to reinforce the gameplay that the mechanic is intended to incentivize. Sometimes this can be very simple. If an add spawns in the encounter and the tank doesn’t establish threat on it quickly, it can melee and endanger other players. The tank needs to pick that add up quickly, which is hopefully fun gameplay for the tank. That’s pretty straightforward. Other times, these penalties can be complex. Let’s use Heroic Ula’tek as an example. If enough individual players don’t contribute to soaking Stone Venom, a player will be affected by Calcified Corpse and very likely wipe the raid. Players need to split into roughly equal groups, react quickly, and ensure that they’re staying with their assigned player until the Stone Venom aura has expired. Calcified Corpse exists only to reinforce gameplay that we want players to enjoy in that phase. “The Punishment Must Fit the Crime” When we design mechanics and their corresponding penalties, it’s important for them to be proportional to each other. items.matters: mimo spadku film pobije wynik Minus One i utwierdza Toho w strategii szybkich sequeli.
items.body: J ohnny Depp is back on top of the box office. Not as a voice in somebody else's franchise, not in a European indie that plays three theaters — as the name above the title of a major studio release, for the first time in eight years. Ebenezer , Paramount's horror-tinged take on A Christmas Carol from X trilogy director Ti West, led the North American box office on Friday with $6.7 million from 3,535 theaters, including $1.5 million from Thursday previews. Depp plays Scrooge; the cast around him runs Rupert Grint as Bob Cratchit, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley and Ian McKellen. It is a PG-13 ghost story wearing a Christmas classic's clothes, and on its first day it beat everything else in the market. The Friday figure is not in dispute — Variety, Deadline and The Hollywood Reporter all report the same $6.7 million. The weekend is where the fight starts. Paramount projects $20 million or better for the three-day frame. The Hollywood Reporter puts it at around $20 million or just under. Variety's range runs $18 to $20 million domestically, with roughly another $20 million expected overseas for a global opening in the $38 to $40 million range. And Deadline, in its Saturday-morning update, recorded the split plainly: Paramount was still holding at $20 million while rival studios saw it coming in lower. That public disagreement is its own story. Studios lowball rivals' numbers every weekend; what matters here is the line both sides are arguing around. Nobody — not even the rivals talking it down — has this movie opening anywhere but No. 1, and nobody has it collapsing. The argument is over whether Depp's comeback opens at $18 million or $20 million. The film cost $38 million to make. For context, that production budget is a fraction of what Depp's studio vehicles used to cost, which is exactly why a number in this range works: Ebenezer does not need to be a phenomenon. It needs to be a solid, profitable hit — and on Friday's evidence, it is on its way to being one. The critics and the audience are telling two different stories. Critics sit at 53% on Rotten Tomatoes — a shrug. The people who actually bought tickets gave the film an A− CinemaScore and 4.5 out of 5 stars on PostTrak, grades that point to the word of mouth a holiday-season release lives on. And The Hollywood Reporter recorded the detail that explains the whole weekend: half of opening-night moviegoers said Depp was their reason for seeing it. That is the comeback question answered in the only currency Hollywood counts. Whatever the industry thought of Depp's drawing power after…

items.headline: How to Rob a Bank David Leitcha otwiera się na ok. 4,7 mln USD przy budżecie 60 mln i ocenie B- w CinemaScore
items.matters: najdroższa wpadka weekendu i sygnał, że gwiazdorska komedia akcji przestała sprzedawać.
items.body: Another over-familiar “family” film title, this one holiday flavored and starring Johnny Depp , takes over the top spot at the box office. Capt. Jack “Ebenezer” is humbugging his way to an opening a bit better than last weekend’s “The Cat in the Hat” reboot. “Cat” cleared $20 — barely. Now deadline.com is taking the $1.5 million the umpteenth version of “A Christmas Carol” managed Thursday and the $5-6 it managed Friday and projecting something in the mid $20s for the whole weekend. That’s not epic, but considering Depp’s quote isn’t what it once was and the budget was in the $40 million range, it’ll do. With tickets averaging over $16 nationwide — over $25 in the Big Cities (JAYZUS), t hat’s not a lot of tickets sold, less than two million. Maybe everybody is waiting to catch it on Tuesday night — bargain night at many of the nation’s cinemas — like me? Sure, it’ll stream long before Christmas rolls in. We’ll wait for that! The newest “Cat in the Hat” is pulling in enough punters to clear $12 million on its second outing, good enough for second place. “Godzilla Minus Zero” opened at over $30 million last weekend , but is falling off a cliff on its second weekend. Friday’s numbers were abysmal, and $8-10 million seems like where this is headed, a 66-70 percent plunge. The Indian release “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” is in the top five (fourth) with a $5 million, earning on a pace with “Cat in the Hat,” which opened the same weekend. The docu-drama “You Can See Everything” is still luring in the curious to see Elizabeth Holmes flirt with her filmmaker/interviewer, adding another $4.5 million or so to its running total, good enough for fifth place. It’s in the $80s , and may fall just shy of $100 million by the time it finishes its run. Jim Caviezel’s “Ghost Soldier” may give it a run for fifth place if it clears $4.9 million on its second weekend. Middling reviews don’t scare off the “Sound of Freedom” faithful that Mel Gibson’s Jesus clings to. But hot on his heels is “How to Rob a Bank,” an all-star (ish) Nicholas Hoult, Zoe Kravitz, Pete Davidson, Christian Slater and John C. Reilly thriller, also tracking towards $4.7 million. Fifth, sixth of seventh, tepid reviews thus far mar this one, too. “Wild Horse Nine,” Martin McDonagh’s latest, amused me and could also be on track to remain in the top ten for one more week. Maybe. “Street Fighter” is done, at last. “Wicker” is fading and “Jimmy” never got any traction. Not enough star power or directorial style to put over a Jimmy Stewart bio-pic. But the much smaller AARP audience is showing up for that…

items.body: Brussels, BELGIUM – The European Commission today proposed its Digital Fairness Act (DFA), aiming to strengthen online consumer protection. While the planned EU-wide regulation might help reduce divergence across EU Member States, it introduces overlapping obligations, parallel enforcement, and unnecessary complexity before current rules have been fully enforced, warns the Computer & Communications Industry Association (CCIA Europe). The recently proposed EU KIDS Act also targets addictive design, further highlighting duplication risks. Moreover, reopening EU consumer law through a 40-article regulation risks further regulatory inflation by EU co-legislators, at odds with the Commission’s recent pledge. Specific measures in today’s proposal raise serious privacy concerns. The DFA’s expanded definition of ‘vulnerable consumers’ now includes personal “misfortune” and circumstances that “impair the consumer’s judgment” – such as addictions and financial distress – while platforms are “reasonably [expected to] foresee” such vulnerabilities, creating legal uncertainty. In practice, this could force digital services to monitor users’ behaviour and process sensitive personal information, conflicting with core GDPR principles such as data minimisation. CCIA Europe urges EU lawmakers to prioritise implementing and enforcing existing laws, alongside cross-border cooperation through the proposed revision of the Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) framework, rather than making the EU rulebook even harder to…

items.headline: Egzekwowanie AI Act trwa od 2 sierpnia 2026: AI Office może nałożyć do 15 mln EUR lub 3 proc. obrotu na dostawców modeli GPAI, do 35 mln EUR lub 7 proc. za praktyki zakazane
items.matters: AI Office nadzoruje też systemy AI wbudowane w platformy wyznaczone jako VLOP.
items.body: Under the EU AI Act, the highest fines can reach €35 million or 7% of a company's total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher, for breaching the bans on prohibited AI practices. Most other breaches can cost up to €15 million or 3%, and supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to authorities up to €7.5 million or 1%. Providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models face a separate regime: since 2 August 2026, the European Commission can fine them up to €15 million or 3%. The figures come from Articles 99 to 101 of the AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 , as amended by the AI Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 , in force since 27 July 2026. They are upper limits, stated as of October 2026; our AI Act section covers new decisions and guidance. The percentage applies when the offender is an undertaking, and it only overtakes the fixed amount for large companies. At a worldwide turnover of €500 million, 7% equals €35 million and 3% equals €15 million; in the 1% tier the crossover point is €750 million. A company with €2 billion in turnover could therefore face up to €140 million for a prohibited practice. For a company that is not an SME and has turnover below €500 million, the fixed €35 million is the ceiling for the same breach. For SMEs, including start-ups, every Article 99 fine is capped at whichever of the two figures is lower . An SME with €20 million in turnover would face at most €1.4 million (7%) for a prohibited practice, not €35 million. Under Recommendation 2003/361/EC , an SME has fewer than 250 staff and turnover of no more than €50 million or a balance sheet total of no more than €43 million. The AI Omnibus extended this relief to small mid-cap enterprises (SMCs), but only in part. The new Article 99(6a) applies the lower cap to SMCs in the €15 million/3% and €7.5 million/1% tiers, not to prohibited practices. Under Recommendation (EU) 2025/1099 , an SMC is not an SME, employs fewer than 750 people and has turnover of up to €150 million or a balance sheet total of up to €129 million. An SMC with €120 million in turnover therefore faces a ceiling of €3.6 million for a breach in the 3% tier, but up to €35 million for a prohibited practice. Providers of general-purpose AI models are supervised by the Commission's AI Office, not by national authorities. items.body: The Digital Services Act (DSA) introduces rules for online services used by European citizens in their everyday life. These services include marketplaces, social media networks, app stores, and online travel and accommodation platforms. The main goal of the DSA is to create a digital space that respects citizens and consumers’ fundamental rights. By establishing a clear set of rules across the EU, the DSA also enables smaller platforms, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and start-ups to scale up in Europe, fostering innovation, growth and competitiveness. The DSA is complemented by the Digital Markets Act (DMA), which includes rules for gatekeeper online platforms. Gatekeepers function as bottlenecks between businesses and consumers for digital services, affecting competition and the functioning of the EU internal market. Some of these services are also covered in the DSA, but for different reasons and with different types of provisions. The DSA empowers citizens by strengthening the protection of their fundamental rights online and giving them greater control and more choices when they navigate online platforms and search engines. The DSA also requires platforms to minimise the risks of exposing citizens, including children and young people, to illegal and harmful content. With the DSA, your digital rights include: The DSA applies to all companies proportionally to their size. The DSA recognises that the biggest online platforms – those with over 45 million monthly users in the EU – play a significant role in our societies and democracies. They must therefore follow specific rules to ensure they do not pose unintentional risks to us, such as amplifying illegal content and shaping opinion at scale, and to minimise the possibility of malicious actors using them to inflict harm on Europe. Once these risks are identified, these larger platforms must put measures in place to reduce them. Similarly, these platforms must meet other requirements to enhance transparency and accountability . A full list of these platforms is published on the Commission’s website. The Commission enforces the DSA together with Digital Services Coordinators – national authorities who supervise the compliance of the platforms established in their territory. The Commission is primarily responsible for the monitoring and enforcement of the additional obligations applying to the biggest platforms and search engines, such as the measures to mitigate systemic risks.
